title: SwarmLoRA: Batched Computation across Isolated Functions for Serverless LoRA Inference
short_description: This artifact reproduces the results for the SC' 26 paper "SwarmLoRA: Batched Computation across Isolated Functions for Serverless LoRA Inference".  The artifacts ...
long_description: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) has enabled over 100,000 adapters for Large Language Models, yet multi-tenant deployments require secure and resilient per-adapter isolation that existing high-throughput systems do not provide. Serverful systems co-locate all adapters in one process for efficient batching but sacrifice isolation; serverless systems run each adapter in an isolated function but redundantly recompute the shared base-model projection in every one, wasting GPU memory bandwidth. We present SwarmLoRA, a disaggregated serverless architecture that separates shared computation from per-adapter state. A persistent aggregator batches the base-model projection once across all active functions; isolated worker functions each hold one adapter's weights and KV cache and scale independently. This design achieves cross-adapter batching without breaking per-adapter isolation. On four L40S GPUs, SwarmLoRA reaches 4.4–5.6× higher throughput than state-of-the-art serverless systems ServerlessLLM and ServerlessLoRA. Under production trace replay it accepts 98–100% of requests across five traffic categories; both comparison systems drop over two-thirds under heavy load. Cold starts complete in 619 ms (2.9× faster than the fastest comparison system), and decode latency holds at 82–87 ms as the adapter pool scales from 10 to 500 mixed-rank adapters on a two-node cluster. SwarmLoRA delivers serverful batching efficiency with secure, resilient, and serverless isolation.

title: RT-HiSS - Ray Tracing Accelerated High Dimensional Vector Similarity Search
short_description: RT-HiSS - Ray Tracing Accelerated High Dimensional Vector Similarity Search
long_description: Recent GPU generations include special-purpose ray tracing (RT) cores for graphics applications. While RT cores are primarily used for rendering, recent works show they can be leveraged for general-purpose tasks, including similarity searches. However, existing approaches do not support datasets exceeding three dimensions. In this work, we propose RT-HiSS, the first exact GPU RT-core-based similarity search algorithm for high-dimensional datasets. GPU similarity search often scales poorly for large datasets with substantial search distances. To address this, RT-HiSS uses RT cores for fast index construction and searches, followed by candidate refinement on CUDA cores. We introduce a two-pass approach to estimate an upper bound on result size, enabling efficient batching under GPU memory constraints with near-perfect load balancing. Additionally, we examine shared memory tiling and compressed result masks to improve GPU resource saturation. Compared to five state-of-the-art GPU algorithms, RT-HiSS achieves significant speedups up to roughly 5,000x.

title: HieraSparse: Hierarchical Semi-Structured Sparse KV Attention
short_description: The artifact of HieraSparse
long_description:
The deployment of long-context Large Language
Models (LLMs) poses significant challenges due to the intense
computational cost of self-attention and the substantial memory
overhead of the Key-Value Cache (KV Cache). In this paper,
we introduce HieraSparse, a hierarchical KV Cache compression
framework with acceleration kernels that leverage GPU sparse
tensor cores to speed up semi-structured KV Cache attention
for both the prefill and decode phases. With the hierarchical
design, our method allows for a flexible quality-sparsity trade-
off and successfully converts sparsity into efficiency. Compared
to the state-of-the-art decode method that utilizes unstructured
sparsity, HieraSparse achieves 1.2×KV compression ratio and
4.57×attention speedup at the same sparsity level. Furthermore,
we extended the semi-structured KV Cache pruning to the prefill
stage, which demonstrated up to 1.85×attention speedup at the
highest sparsity. Lastly, we evaluate the generation quality of
HieraSparse with a simple magnitude-based pruning method, and
the results show that 1.37×prefill speedup and 1.77×decode
speedup can be achieved without significant quality drop. The
codebase can be found at https://github.com/psl-ntu/HieraSparse.

title: Artifact Reproduction: Lightweight, Modular Verification for WebAssembly-to-Native Instruction Selection (Crocus, ASPLOS '24)
short_description: Chameleon reproduction of the ASPLOS '24 Crocus artifact by VanHattum et al.: formal verification of Cranelift's instruction-lowering rules for compiling WebAssembly to native ARM aarch64.
long_description:
## Overview

This artifact reproduces the evaluation from **"Lightweight, Modular
Verification for WebAssembly-to-Native Instruction Selection"** (Crocus) by
Alexa VanHattum, Monica Pardeshi, Chris Fallin, Adrian Sampson, and Fraser
Brown, published at ASPLOS '24.

Language-level guarantees like WebAssembly's module isolation are only as
strong as the compiler that lowers Wasm bytecode to native machine code.
Crocus is a system for lightweight, modular verification of instruction-
lowering rules inside Cranelift — a production, retargetable Wasm native
code generator used by Wasmtime and other runtimes. Crocus lifts Cranelift's
ISLE lowering rules and ISA semantics into SMT queries, checking that each
rule's right-hand side is equivalent to (and applicable under the same
conditions as) its left-hand side. The paper applies Crocus to lowering
rules covering WebAssembly 1.0 integer operations for the ARM aarch64
backend, and reports bugs uncovered in the process.

## What this artifact reproduces

- Building Crocus (the modified Cranelift + verification harness)
- Running the SMT-based verification queries over the covered ISLE rules
- Reproducing the rule-coverage and verification-outcome tables from the
  paper

## Environment

- Platform: Chameleon Cloud (CHI@TACC)
- Node: bare-metal ARM (compute_arm64)
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 ARM
- Dependencies: Rust toolchain, Z3, and the pinned Cranelift fork; installed
  by the setup notebook

> Note on architecture: the upstream artifact's Docker image is built for
> `arm64`, so it does **not** run on Chameleon's default x86_64 nodes.
> This reproduction targets a native aarch64 Chameleon node so that the
> image and the ISA under verification match.

## How to run

1. Open `crocus_reproduction_tacc.ipynb` to execute the verification queries and
   reproduce the paper's main tables.

## References

- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3617232.3624862
- Upstream artifact: https://github.com/avanhatt/asplos24-ae-crocus
- Original authors: Alexa VanHattum, Monica Pardeshi (Cornell/Wellesley),
  Chris Fallin (Fastly), Adrian Sampson (Cornell), Fraser Brown
  (CMU/Stanford)

title: Artifact Reproduction: Early Termination for Hyperdimensional Computing Using Inferential Statistics (ASPLOS '25)
short_description: Chameleon reproduction of the ASPLOS '25 artifact by Yi et al.: uses inferential statistics to terminate Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) inference early with bounded accuracy loss.
long_description:
## Overview

This artifact reproduces the evaluation from **"Early Termination for
Hyperdimensional Computing Using Inferential Statistics"** by Pu (Luke) Yi,
Yifan Yang, Chae Young Lee, and Sara Achour (Stanford University), published
at ASPLOS '25.

Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) is a brain-inspired, lightweight
classification paradigm well-suited to edge and emerging-hardware deployments.
Because HDC inference is error-resilient and its hypervector dimensions are
exchangeable, classification can be terminated before all dimensions are
processed, trading off a small, statistically bounded accuracy loss for
reduced latency. The paper introduces an *inferential-statistics-based*
early-termination scheme that provides principled accuracy guarantees at
runtime rather than relying on ad-hoc heuristics.

## What this artifact reproduces

- End-to-end HDC inference pipelines on the datasets used in the paper
- The early-termination decision procedure and its accuracy/latency tradeoff
- Comparison against baseline (full-dimension) HDC inference

## Environment

- Platform: Chameleon Cloud (CHI@UC), x86_64 bare-metal node
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 (via provided Chameleon image)
- Dependencies: installed automatically via the setup notebook

> Note: the original upstream Docker image was published for `arm64`. This
> artifact runs natively on x86_64 Chameleon hardware; the setup builds the
> environment from source rather than pulling the arm64 image.

## How to run

1. Open `omen_reproduction.ipynb` and run the cells to install dependencies and execute the artifact.

## References

- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3669940.3707254
- Original authors: Pu (Luke) Yi, Yifan Yang, Chae Young Lee, Sara Achour
  (Stanford University)

title: Paralegal Performance Benchmark
short_description: Reproduces the Paralegal (OSDI '25) performance benchmarks on a Chameleon bare-metal node using the authors' frozen Docker image, and generates the paper's plots.
long_description:
This artifact reproduces the performance benchmarks of Paralegal, the static Rust privacy/security analyzer from the OSDI '25 paper "Paralegal: Practical Static Analysis for Privacy Bugs."

The included Jupyter notebook runs the full experiment on Chameleon Cloud: it reserves a single Intel x86_64 bare-metal node (compute_cascadelake_r at CHI@UC), installs Docker, and downloads and loads the authors' frozen Docker image from Zenodo (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15374862). It then runs the performance benchmark (the "griswold" coordinator) over the case-study applications and generates the paper's figures with the artifact's own plotting/plot.py, all inside the container. The benchmark runs detached so it survives SSH disconnects, and the figures are bind-mounted back to the host, fetched into the notebook, and displayed inline. The notebook releases the Chameleon resources when finished.

Using the authors' frozen Docker image (rather than building from source) pins the exact Rust toolchain and crate versions, so the experiment reproduces reliably despite newer, incompatible crate releases on crates.io that break a from-source build of the pinned toolchain.

Outputs include ide_ci_plot.png, per_controller_plot.png, k_depth_plot.png, old_adaptive_plot.png, and dependency_times.txt, generated by the artifact's plot.py.

Hardware: 1x Intel x86_64 bare-metal node (no GPU). Runtime: roughly 90 minutes for the benchmark, plus image download (~3 GB) and case-study build time. Original artifact: https://github.com/brownsys/paralegal-osdi-2025-artifact

short_description: Scaled Chameleon/Trovi reproduction of the HPDC ’24 context-reuse experiments for function-centric applications.
long_description:
This artifact reproduces a scaled version of the ACM HPDC ’24 paper “Accelerating Function-Centric Applications by Discovering, Distributing, and Retaining Reusable Context in Workflow Systems.”

The reproduction focuses on the paper’s LNNI-style context-reuse evaluation. It compares three execution modes: L1 with no context reuse, L2 with disk-level context reuse, and L3 with disk and memory context reuse. The goal is to reproduce the main systems trend that repeated function invocations become faster when reusable context is retained on workers.

title: bpftime Userspace Uprobe Benchmark: OSDI '25 Reproduction on Chameleon
short_description: Reproduces the userspace-vs-kernel uprobe latency benchmark from bpftime (OSDI '25) on a Chameleon Intel bare-metal node, with plots of the measured speedup.
long_description:
This artifact reproduces the core micro-benchmark behind bpftime, the userspace eBPF runtime from the OSDI '25 paper "Extending Applications Safely and Efficiently" (Zheng et al.). bpftime runs eBPF programs such as uprobes in userspace, avoiding the kernel-userspace context switch that traditional kernel uprobes incur on every probe hit.

The included Jupyter notebook performs an end-to-end run on Chameleon Cloud: it reserves a single Intel x86_64 bare-metal node (compute_cascadelake_r at CHI@UC), installs build dependencies, clones and builds bpftime with the uprobe benchmark, and runs the micro-benchmark over SSH. It measures average per-probe latency for uprobe, uretprobe, and combined uprobe+uretprobe under both the kernel eBPF path and the bpftime userspace runtime, then fetches the results back and plots (1) kernel vs. userspace latency and (2) the measured speedup per probe type.

The notebook is self-contained and idempotent (it reuses an existing lease/server if present) and cleans up its Chameleon resources at the end.

Hardware: 1x Intel x86_64 bare-metal node (no GPU). Runtime: roughly 40-60 minutes including build. Original code: https://github.com/eunomia-bpf/bpftime

title: vAttention Reproduction on Chameleon (Mechanism, Turing RTX 6000)
short_description: Reproduces the core mechanism of vAttention: Dynamic Memory Management for Serving LLMs without PagedAttention (Prabhu et al., ASPLOS 2025).
long_description:
## What this artifact reproduces

- The vAttention dynamic memory allocator builds and runs on Turing hardware
- `vattn_demo_sync.py` measures per-step synchronous allocation overhead
- `vattn_demo_async.py` validates the async optimization (pass 2 ≪ pass 1)

## What this artifact does NOT reproduce

The paper's end-to-end serving benchmarks (`benchmark_e2e_static_trace.py`, `benchmark_e2e_dynamic_trace.py`) require an Ampere or newer GPU (compute capability ≥ 8.0). FlashAttention 2.5.9 — the version pinned by the paper — has a hard runtime check that rejects sm_75 (Turing) and below. This artifact runs only the allocator-level experiments, which use standard CUDA virtual memory APIs and work on Turing.

To extend this artifact to the full paper, change `NODE_TYPE = "compute_gigaio"` (A100) in Cell 3 of the notebook and re-run.

## Hardware target

- **Site**: CHI@UC
- **Node type**: `gpu_rtx_6000` (default) or `compute_gigaio` for full paper
- **Image**: `CC-Ubuntu22.04-CUDA`
- **Lease duration**: 2 hours recommended

## Expected results (Turing RTX 6000)

| Mode | Per-step overhead |
|---|---|
| Synchronous | ~7-8 ms |
| Async pass 1 (warmup) | ~0.6 ms |
| Async pass 2 (steady state) | ~0.05 ms |
| Speedup sync vs async pass 2 | **~150×** |

## How to run

1. Click "Launch on Chameleon" above
2. Open `vattention-reproduction.ipynb`
3. Edit Cell 1's `chi.set("project_name", ...)` to your project
4. Run all cells (Kernel → Restart Kernel and Run All Cells)
5. Total runtime ~45 minutes on a fresh instance (sarathi-lean build dominates)

## Citation

```bibtex
@misc{prabhu2024vattention,
  title={vAttention: Dynamic Memory Management for Serving LLMs without PagedAttention},
  author={Ramya Prabhu and Ajay Nayak and Jayashree Mohan and Ramachandran Ramjee and Ashish Panwar},
  year={2024},
  url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.04437}
}
```

Original code: https://github.com/microsoft/vattention

title: Reproduction of StreamingLLM (Xiao et al., ICLR 2024) on Pythia-1.4B
short_description: End-to-end Chameleon GPU reproduction of StreamingLLM (Xiao et al., ICLR 2024, Fig. 3) on Pythia-1.4B + WikiText-2. Dense baseline shows 806× PPL degradation past the 2048-token context window.
long_description:
This Trovi reproduces the central experiment (Figure 3) of:
  Xiao, G., Tian, Y., Chen, B., Han, S., Lewis, M.
  "Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks." ICLR 2024.
  https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.17453

When run end-to-end on Chameleon Cloud the notebook:
1. Leases a gpu_rtx_6000 baremetal node at CHI@UC.
2. Installs Miniconda + Python 3.8 + transformers==4.33.0 + the upstream streaming_llm package.
3. Runs a custom inline perplexity loop on Pythia-1.4B-deduped + WikiText-2 twice:
   - StreamingLLM (4 attention sinks + 2000 recent tokens, position-shift attention)
   - Dense baseline (full KV cache, no eviction)
4. Plots per-token PPL (raw + 128-token rolling mean) on a log-y axis.
5. Releases all Chameleon resources automatically.

Why a custom eval (not examples/eval_long_ppl.py)?
The upstream evaluator hard-codes a check for Llama and raises ValueError for any other model
type. Llama-2 needs HuggingFace gating that would block reviewers, so we use Pythia (gpt_neox)
and call streaming_llm.enable_streaming_llm + streaming_llm.pos_shift.modify_gpt_neox directly.
This keeps the Trovi self-contained with no external account requirements.

Key results (8192-token sequences from WikiText-2 validation):
  StreamingLLM mean PPL: 8.91
  Dense baseline mean PPL: 626.00
  At token position 8000: StreamingLLM ~1100, Dense ~888,000 → 806x degradation
Hardware / cost: ~1 hour wall-clock on gpu_rtx_6000 (24GB) at CHI@UC. ~1–2 SU.

Reproducibility notes:

1.All Python package versions pinned in Step 2.

2.streaming-llm commit pinned in the notebook (HEAD as of May 22, 2026: 2e504260).

3.The lease/server are deleted in the final cell — no SU leak even if the run fails.

Built as part of the SYAIR-Repro computing-education project at UChicago CS/PSD (PI: Prof. Haryadi Gunawi), using Chameleon allocation CHI-251412.

title: Aesthetic Hub Serving (Nvidia)
short_description: This lab benchmarks and optimizes a two-stage image aesthetic scoring pipeline on NVIDIA GPU hardware (A100/A30) and AMD EPYC 7763 CPU.
long_description:
### Model Optimizations for Aesthetic Score Prediction

This lab benchmarks and optimizes a two-stage image aesthetic scoring pipeline on NVIDIA GPU hardware (A100/A30) and AMD EPYC 7763 CPU. It can be accessed [here](https://trovi.chameleoncloud.org/dashboard/artifacts/c347ab71-1a5b-41cf-a2fd-0c34d30f1e1d/).

#### Pipeline

```
Image (~500×500 Flickr JPG) → Resize/CenterCrop to 224×224
    → CLIP ViT-L/14 (304M params, frozen, GPU) → 768-dim embedding
    → Global MLP (~430K params) → scalar aesthetic score (0–1)
    → Personalized MLP (~430K params + user embeddings) → per-user aesthetic score (0–1)
```

- **CLIP ViT-L/14**: A frozen Vision Transformer that generates 768-dimensional image embeddings. Benchmarked on latency and throughput across batch sizes on both CPU and GPU (eager vs compiled mode).
- **Global MLP**: A lightweight feed-forward network (768→512→128→32→1 with sigmoid) that predicts a universal aesthetic score.
- **Personalized MLP**: Takes a 768-dim CLIP embedding + 64-dim learned user embedding (832 total) and predicts a per-user aesthetic score.

#### Dataset

Flickr-AES (ICCV 2017 Aesthetics Dataset) — ~40K Flickr images with crowd-sourced aesthetic ratings, hosted on Google Drive. Split manifests (`flickr_global_manifest.csv`, `flickr_personalized_manifest.csv`) define train/val/test/production splits. Data is downloaded via `gdown` into a Docker volume.

#### What this lab covers

1. **Data preparation**: Downloading the Flickr-AES dataset from Google Drive into a Docker volume using `gdown`.
2. **PyTorch baseline**: Measuring ViT encoder latency/throughput (eager vs compiled, CPU and GPU) and MLP inference latency/throughput on CPU. End-to-end pipeline timing on both CPU and GPU.
3. **ONNX conversion**: Exporting the MLP heads to ONNX format.
4. **ONNX optimization**: Graph optimizations, dynamic and static quantization on the MLP models.
5. **Execution providers**: Testing the MLP ONNX models with CPUExecutionProvider, CUDAExecutionProvider, TensorrtExecutionProvider, and OpenVINOExecutionProvider.
6. **FastAPI serving**: Deploying the optimized MLP heads as a REST API (FastAPI + ONNX Runtime GPU) with four endpoints (global/personalized × single/batch). Benchmarked for latency and throughput under sequential and concurrent load.
7. **Triton Inference Server**: Serving both models via NVIDIA Triton (ONNX backend). Benchmarked with the Python `tritonclient`, `perf_analyzer` concurrency/batch sweeps, multi-instance scaling, and dynamic batching.

#### Hardware

This lab uses NVIDIA GPU nodes on Chameleon Cloud:

- `compute_liqid` nodes at CHI@TACC — NVIDIA A100 40GB + AMD EPYC 7763 CPU
- `compute_gigaio` nodes at CHI@UC — NVIDIA A100 80GB + AMD EPYC 7763 CPU

title: MPI bare-metal cluster
short_description: This appliance deploys an MPI cluster composed of bare metal instances using the MVAPICH2 library over InfiniBand.
long_description:
This appliance deploys an MPI cluster composed of bare metal instances using the MVAPICH2 library over InfiniBand.

This appliance accepts the following parameters:

key_name: name of a key pair to enable SSH access to the instance (defaults to "default")
reservation_id: ID of the Blazar reservation to use for launching instances
node_count: Number of physical nodes to launch
The following outputs are provided:

first_instance_ip: The public IP address of the first bare-metal instance. Login with the command 'ssh cc@first_instance_ip'.
deployment_results: The private IPs and hostnames of all deployed instances
To run MPI programs, execute the following command, assuming you have compiled a program called mpi.out:

mpirun_rsh -np <nprocs> -hostfile hosts ./mpi.out
Refer to the [MVAPICH2 user guide](https://mvapich.cse.ohio-state.edu/userguide/) for more details on running MPI programs.

To compiling an MPI program, use a command such as this one:

mpicc -o hello_world hello_world.c


MVAPICH2

authors.affiliation: Network Based Computing Lab, The Ohio State University

environment_setup.arguments:
heat_template_version: 2015-10-15

description: Bare-metal MPI cluster using the MVAPICH2 library.
             Please make sure that you have leased a set of nodes with InfiniBand
             support before launching this complex appliance.

parameters:
  key_name:
    type: string
    label: Key name
    description: Name of a key pair to enable SSH access to the instance
    default: default
    constraints:
    - custom_constraint: nova.keypair
  reservation_id:
    type: string
    description: ID of the Blazar reservation to use for launching instances
    constraints:
    - custom_constraint: blazar.reservation

  node_count:
    type: number
    label: Node count
    description: Number of physical nodes
    default: 1
    constraints:
      - range: { min: 1 }
        description: There must be at least one physical node.

resources:
  mpi_keypair:
    type: OS::Nova::KeyPair
    properties:
      save_private_key: true
      name:
        str_replace:
          template: mpi_stack_id
          params:
            stack_id: { get_param: "OS::stack_id" }

  instance_floating_ip:
    type: OS::Nova::FloatingIP
    properties:
      pool: public

  instance_association:
    type: OS::Nova::FloatingIPAssociation
    properties:
      floating_ip: { get_resource: instance_floating_ip }
      server_id: { get_attr: [mpi_cluster, resource.0] }

  export_hosts:
    type: OS::Heat::SoftwareConfig
    properties:
      outputs:
        - name: hosts
      group: script
      config: |
        #!/bin/sh
        (echo -n $(facter ipaddress); echo -n ' '; echo $(facter hostname)) > ${heat_outputs_path}.hosts

  export_hosts_sdg:
    type: OS::Heat::SoftwareDeploymentGroup
    properties:
      config: { get_resource: export_hosts }
      servers: { get_attr: [mpi_cluster, refs_map] }
      signal_transport: HEAT_SIGNAL

  populate_hosts:
    type: OS::Heat::SoftwareConfig
    properties:
      inputs:
        - name: hosts
      group: script
      config: |
        #!/usr/bin/env python
        import ast
        import os
        import string
        import subprocess
        hosts = os.getenv('hosts')
        if hosts is not None:
            hosts = ast.literal_eval(string.replace(hosts, '\n', '\\n'))
        with open('/etc/hosts', 'a') as hosts_file:
          for ip_host in hosts.values():
              hosts_file.write(ip_host.rstrip() + '\n')

  populate_hosts_sdg:
    type: OS::Heat::SoftwareDeploymentGroup
    depends_on: export_hosts_sdg
    properties:
      config: { get_resource: populate_hosts }
      servers: { get_attr: [mpi_cluster, refs_map] }
      signal_transport: HEAT_SIGNAL
      input_values:
        hosts: { get_attr: [ export_hosts_sdg, hosts ] }

  mpi_cluster:
    type: OS::Heat::ResourceGroup
    properties:
      count: { get_param: node_count }
      resource_def:
        type: OS::Nova::Server
        properties:
          name: mpi-instance-%index%
          image: DIB-OSU-CentOS7-SRIOV-MVAPICH2
          flavor: baremetal
          key_name: { get_param: key_name }
          networks:
             - network: sharednet1
          scheduler_hints: { reservation: { get_param: reservation_id } }
          user_data_format: SOFTWARE_CONFIG
          software_config_transport: POLL_SERVER_HEAT

          user_data:
            str_replace:
              template: |
                #!/bin/bash
                # disable HT
                for CPU in `seq 24 47`
                do
                   echo "0" > /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu$CPU/online;
                done
                sudo yum -y install wget

                # Take care of access key for instance
                cd /home/cc/.ssh/
                cat << EOF > id_rsa.pub
                public_key
                EOF
                cat << EOF > id_rsa
                private_key
                EOF
                cat << EOF > config
                Host *
                  StrictHostKeyChecking no
                EOF
                cat id_rsa.pub >> authorized_keys
                chmod 600 authorized_keys id_rsa
                chmod 644 id_rsa.pub config
                sudo chown cc:cc *

                cd /home/cc/
                for i in `seq 0 $(( node_count - 1 ))`
                do
                    echo mpi-instance-$i >> hosts
                done
                sudo chown cc:cc hosts
                # Detect and install MVAPICH2 library
                /root/mv2-chameleon.sh

              params:
                node_count: { get_param: node_count }
                private_key: { get_attr: [ mpi_keypair, private_key ] }
                public_key: { get_attr: [ mpi_keypair, public_key ] }

outputs:
    first_instance_ip:
      description: The public IP address of the first instance. Login with the command 'ssh cc@first_instance_ip'.
      value: { get_attr: [instance_floating_ip, ip] }
    deployment_results:
      description: The private IPs and hostnames of all deployed instances
      value: { get_attr: [export_hosts_sdg, hosts] }

title: MPI+Spack Bare Metal Cluster
short_description: This template sets up an HPC cluster with master and worker nodes, with MPI (MPICH and OpenMPI) and Spack available.
long_description:
Appliance Parameters
- reservation_id: ID of the Blazar reservation for master and worker nodes.
- bootstrapnode_reservation_id: ID of the Blazar reservation for the bootstrap node.
- network_name: Name of the network.
- image_name: Name of the image to be used by the cluster. Must be one of the following: Ubuntu22.04-HPC-MPI-Spack, Ubuntu22.04-HPC-MPI-Spack-CUDA, or Ubuntu22.04-HPC-MPI-Spack-ROCm. Defaults to Ubuntu22.04-HPC-MPI-Spack.
- worker_count: Number of worker nodes. Defaults to 1.
- spack_packages: List of additional Spack packages to install.
- private_key_content: Contents of the SSH private key.
- public_key_content: Contents of the SSH public key, allowing login into instances.

Outputs Provided
- master_ip: Floating IP of the master node.
- keypair_name: Name of the MPI keypair used.

Stack Creation via OpenStack CLI
- You can create the stack using the following commands and variables:

SSH_KEY=/work/.ssh/id_rsa    # Path to the SSH key file that will be used as the cluster's keypair
STACK_NAME=mpi-stack
NETWORK_NAME=sharednet1
IMAGE_NAME=Ubuntu22.04-HPC-MPI-Spack
RESERVATION_ID=""            # Enter the reservation id
BOOTSTRAP_RESERVATION_ID=""  # Enter the bootstrap reservation id
WORKER_COUNT=1               # Number of worker nodes
SPACK_PACKAGES="pdsh,zlib"   # Comma-separated list of extra spack packages to be installed on all nodes

openstack stack create ${STACK_NAME} -t template.yml --wait \
  --parameter-file private_key_content=${SSH_KEY} \
  --parameter-file public_key_content=${SSH_KEY}.pub \
  --parameter network_name=${NETWORK_NAME} \
  --parameter image_name=${IMAGE_NAME} \
  --parameter bootstrapnode_reservation_id=${BOOTSTRAP_RESERVATION_ID} \
  --parameter reservation_id=${RESERVATION_ID} \
  --parameter worker_count=${WORKER_COUNT} \
  --parameter spack_packages=${SPACK_PACKAGES}

environment_setup.arguments:
heat_template_version: 2021-04-16

description: HPC cluster setup with Spack and MPI for deploying and configuring master and worker nodes via a bootstrap node.

parameters:
  bootstrapnode_reservation_id:
    type: string
    description: ID of the Blazar reservation for bootstrap node
    constraints:
      - custom_constraint: blazar.reservation

  reservation_id:
    type: string
    description: ID of the Blazar reservation for master/workers
    constraints:
      - custom_constraint: blazar.reservation

  network_name:
    type: string
    description: Network name (should be an existing one eg.sharednet1)
    constraints:
      - custom_constraint: neutron.network

  image_name:
    type: string
    description: Image Name to be used by the cluster
    default: Ubuntu22.04-HPC-MPI-Spack

  worker_count:
    type: number
    description: Number of worker nodes
    default: 1

  spack_packages:
    type: comma_delimited_list
    description: List of Spack packages to install
    default: [ pdsh ]

  private_key_content:
    type: string
    description: SSH private key contents

  public_key_content:
    type: string
    description: SSH public key content, allows logging into instances
 
  nfs_share_size:
    type: number
    description: Size of the NFS Share(nfs_mpi_share) which will be mounted at /nfs 
    default: 0
    constraints:
      - range: { min: 0 }

conditions:
  create_nfs_share: { not: { equals: [ { get_param: nfs_share_size }, 0 ] } }

resources:
  mpi_keypair:
    type: OS::Nova::KeyPair
    properties:
      name:
        list_join:
          - '-'
          - - { get_param: OS::stack_name }
            - keypair
      public_key: { get_param: public_key_content }

  bootstrap_node:
    type: OS::Nova::Server
    properties:
      name: mpi-bootstrap
      flavor: baremetal
      image: Ubuntu22.04-HPC-MPI-Spack
      key_name: { get_resource: mpi_keypair }
      networks:
        - network: sharednet1
      scheduler_hints: { reservation: { get_param: bootstrapnode_reservation_id } }
      user_data_format: RAW
      user_data:
        str_replace:
          template: |
            #!/bin/bash
            set -e

            mkdir -p /work/.ssh
            chown cc:cc /work/.ssh
            chmod 700 /work/.ssh

            cat > /work/.ssh/id_rsa <<EOF
            PRIVATE_KEY
            EOF

            cat > /work/.ssh/id_rsa.pub <<EOF
            PUBLIC_KEY
            EOF

            chmod 600 /work/.ssh/id_rsa
            chmod 644 /work/.ssh/id_rsa.pub
            chown -R cc:cc /work/.ssh

            apt-get update
            apt-get install -y git ansible

            cd /home/cc
            git clone https://github.com/pmodels/cc-hpc-appliances.git mpi-ansible
            cd mpi-ansible

            cat > inventory.ini <<EOF
            [master_node]
            MASTER_NAME ansible_host=MASTER_IP

            [worker_nodes]
            EOF

            IFS=',' read -r -a NAMES <<< "WORKER_NAMES"
            IFS=',' read -r -a IPS <<< "WORKER_IPS"
            for i in "${!NAMES[@]}"; do
              echo "${NAMES[$i]} ansible_host=${IPS[$i]}" >> inventory.ini
            done

            cat >> inventory.ini <<EOF
            [worker_nodes:vars]
            ansible_ssh_common_args='-o ProxyJump=cc@MASTER_IP'
            EOF
                        
            if [ -n "NFS_SHARE" ]; then
                EXPORT=$(echo "NFS_SHARE" | sed "s/[][]//g" | sed "s/'//g")
                NFS_LIST="[{'mount':'/nfs','export':'$EXPORT'}]"        
            else
                NFS_LIST="[]"
            fi
                        
            export ANSIBLE_PYTHON_INTERPRETER=/usr/bin/python3
            export ANSIBLE_SSH_ARGS="-F /home/cc/mpi-ansible/config"
            
            ansible-playbook -i ./inventory.ini -e "spack_packages=['SPACK_PACKAGES']" -e "nfs_shares='$NFS_LIST'" ./mpi-cluster.yml

          params:
            MASTER_NAME: { get_attr: [ master_node, name ] }
            MASTER_IP: { get_attr: [ master_floating_ip, ip ] }
            WORKER_NAMES: { list_join: [ ",", { get_attr: [ worker_nodes, name ] } ] }
            WORKER_IPS: { list_join: [ ",", { get_attr: [ worker_nodes, first_address ] } ] }
            PUBLIC_KEY: { get_param: public_key_content }
            PRIVATE_KEY: { get_param: private_key_content }
            SPACK_PACKAGES: { list_join: [ "','", { get_param: spack_packages } ] }
            NFS_SHARE:
              if:
                - create_nfs_share
                - { get_attr: [ nfs_share, export_locations ] }
                - ""

  master_node:
    type: OS::Nova::Server
    properties:
      name: mpi-master-node
      flavor: baremetal
      image: { get_param: image_name }
      key_name: { get_resource: mpi_keypair }
      networks:
        - network: { get_param: network_name }
      scheduler_hints: { reservation: { get_param: reservation_id } }

  worker_nodes:
    type: OS::Heat::ResourceGroup
    properties:
      count: { get_param: worker_count }
      resource_def:
        type: OS::Nova::Server
        properties:
          name: mpi-worker-node-%index%
          flavor: baremetal
          image: { get_param: image_name }
          key_name: { get_resource: mpi_keypair }
          networks:
            - network: { get_param: network_name }
          scheduler_hints: { reservation: { get_param: reservation_id } }

  nfs_share:
    type: OS::Manila::Share
    condition: create_nfs_share
    properties:
      name: mpi_nfs_share
      share_protocol: NFS
      size: { get_param: nfs_share_size }

  master_floating_ip:
    type: OS::Nova::FloatingIP
    properties:
      pool: public

  master_floating_ip_association:
    type: OS::Nova::FloatingIPAssociation
    properties:
      floating_ip: { get_resource: master_floating_ip }
      server_id: { get_resource: master_node }

outputs:
  master_ip:
    description: Floating IP of the Master node
    value: { get_attr: [ master_floating_ip, ip ] }

  keypair_name:
    description: Name of the MPI KeyPair used
    value: { get_resource: mpi_keypair }

This template can be used to create a layer2 network that stitches to ExoGENI. It does not create any nodes and only creates the network that can be used by other nodes created in the future.

Note that the template can be modified to create both the network and nodes for an experiment.

environment_setup.arguments:
# This describes what is deployed by this template.
description: This template creates a ExoGENI stitchable network without any nodes attached to it.

      name: router

        network: public

  subnet:
    type: OS::Neutron::Subnet
    properties:
      name: subnet
      cidr: { get_param: ip_subnet }
      enable_dhcp: true
      network: { get_resource: network }

  network:
    type: OS::Neutron::ProviderNet
    properties:
      network_type: vlan
      physical_network: exogeni
      name: { get_param: network_name }
      shared: false

  router_interface:
    type: OS::Neutron::RouterInterface
    properties:
      router: { get_resource: router_to_ext }
      subnet: { get_resource: subnet }

# The parameters section gathers configuration from the user.
parameters:
  network_name:
    type: string
    description: Name of the network to use.
  ip_subnet:
    type: string
    description: Cidr of the network
    default: 192.168.100.0/24

# This describes what is deployed by this template.
description: This template creates a ExoGENI stitchable network without any nodes attached to it.

# This defines the minimum Heat version required by this template.
heat_template_version: 2015-10-15

# The resources section defines what OpenStack resources are to be deployed and
# how they should be configured.
resources:
  router_to_ext:
    type: OS::Neutron::Router
    properties:
      name: router
      external_gateway_info:
        network: public

  subnet:
    type: OS::Neutron::Subnet
    properties:

resources:

title: MPICH 4.2.3 bare-metal cluster
short_description: This appliance deploys a MPI cluster composed of bare metal instances using the MPICH implementation.
long_description:
This appliance deploys a MPI cluster composed of bare metal instances using the MPICH implementation. A hostfile is automatically generated and provided to MPICH to utilize the available instances.

This appliance accepts the following parameters:

key_name: name of a key pair to enable SSH access to the instance (defaults to "default")
reservation_id: ID of the Blazar reservation to use for launching instances
node_count: Number of physical nodes to launch
The following outputs are provided:

first_instance_ip: The public IP address of the first bare-metal instance. Login with the command 'ssh cc@first_instance_ip'.
deployment_results: The private IPs and hostnames of all deployed instances
To compile an MPI program, use a command such as this one:

mpicc mpi_hello.c -o mpi_hello
To run MPI programs, execute the following command, assuming you have compiled a program called mpi_hello:

mpiexec -n <nprocs> ./mpi_hello

MPI

environment_setup.arguments:
heat_template_version: 2015-10-15

description: Bare-metal MPI cluster using the MPICH implementation

parameters:
  key_name:
    type: string
    label: Key name
    description: Name of a key pair to enable SSH access to the instance
    default: default
    constraints:
    - custom_constraint: nova.keypair
  reservation_id:
    type: string
    description: ID of the Blazar reservation to use for launching instances
    constraints:
    - custom_constraint: blazar.reservation

  node_count:
    type: number
    label: Node count
    description: Number of physical nodes
    default: 1
    constraints:
      - range: { min: 1 }
        description: There must be at least one physical node.

resources:
  mpi_keypair:
    type: OS::Nova::KeyPair
    properties:
      save_private_key: true
      name:
        str_replace:
          template: mpi_stack_id
          params:
            stack_id: { get_param: "OS::stack_id" }

  instance_floating_ip:
    type: OS::Nova::FloatingIP
    properties:
      pool: public

  instance_association:
    type: OS::Nova::FloatingIPAssociation
    properties:
      floating_ip: { get_resource: instance_floating_ip }
      server_id: { get_attr: [mpi_cluster, resource.0] }

  export_hosts:
    type: OS::Heat::SoftwareConfig
    properties:
      outputs:
        - name: hosts
      group: script
      config: |
        #!/bin/sh
        (echo -n $(hostname -i); echo -n ' '; echo $(hostname)) > ${heat_outputs_path}.hosts

  export_hosts_sdg:
    type: OS::Heat::SoftwareDeploymentGroup
    properties:
      config: { get_resource: export_hosts }
      servers: { get_attr: [mpi_cluster, refs_map] }
      signal_transport: HEAT_SIGNAL

  populate_hosts:
    type: OS::Heat::SoftwareConfig
    properties:
      inputs:
        - name: hosts
      group: script
      config: |
        #!/usr/bin/env python
        import ast
        import os
        import subprocess
        hosts = os.getenv('hosts')
        if hosts is not None:
            hosts = ast.literal_eval(hosts.replace('\n', '\\n'))
        with open('/etc/hosts', 'a') as hosts_file:
          for ip_host in hosts.values():
              hosts_file.write(ip_host.rstrip() + '\n')

  populate_hosts_sdg:
    type: OS::Heat::SoftwareDeploymentGroup
    depends_on: export_hosts_sdg
    properties:
      config: { get_resource: populate_hosts }
      servers: { get_attr: [mpi_cluster, refs_map] }
      signal_transport: HEAT_SIGNAL
      input_values:
        hosts: { get_attr: [ export_hosts_sdg, hosts ] }

  mpi_cluster:
    type: OS::Heat::ResourceGroup
    properties:
      count: { get_param: node_count }
      resource_def:
        type: OS::Nova::Server
        properties:
          name: mpi-instance-%index%
          image: MPICH-4.2.1
          flavor: baremetal
          key_name: { get_param: key_name }
          networks:
             - network: sharednet1
          scheduler_hints: { reservation: { get_param: reservation_id } }
          user_data_format: SOFTWARE_CONFIG
          software_config_transport: POLL_SERVER_HEAT

          user_data:
            str_replace:
              template: |
                #!/bin/bash

                # Take care of access key for instance
                cd /home/cc/.ssh/
                cat << EOF > id_rsa.pub
                public_key
                EOF
                cat << EOF > id_rsa
                private_key
                EOF
                cat << EOF > config
                Host *
                  StrictHostKeyChecking no
                EOF
                cat id_rsa.pub >> authorized_keys
                chmod 600 authorized_keys id_rsa
                chmod 644 id_rsa.pub config
                sudo chown cc:cc *

                cd /home/cc/
                for i in `seq 0 $(( node_count - 1 ))`
                do
                    echo mpi-instance-$i.novalocal >> hosts
                done
                sudo chown cc:cc hosts

                echo "export HYDRA_HOST_FILE=/home/cc/hosts" >> .bash_profile

              params:
                node_count: { get_param: node_count }
                private_key: { get_attr: [ mpi_keypair, private_key ] }
                public_key: { get_attr: [ mpi_keypair, public_key ] }

outputs:
    first_instance_ip:
      description: The public IP address of the first instance. Login with the command 'ssh cc@first_instance_ip'.
      value: { get_attr: [instance_floating_ip, ip] }
    deployment_results:
      description: The private IPs and hostnames of all deployed instances
      value: { get_attr: [export_hosts_sdg, hosts] }

          template: mpi_stack_id
          params:
            stack_id: { get_param: "OS::stack_id" }

  instance_floating_ip:
    type: OS::Nova::FloatingIP
    properties:
      pool: public

  instance_association:
    type: OS::Nova::FloatingIPAssociation
    properties:
      floating_ip: { get_resource: instance_floating_ip }
      server_id: { get_attr: [mpi_cluster, resource.0] }

  export_hosts:
    type: OS::Heat::SoftwareConfig
    properties:
      outputs:
        - name: hosts
      group: script
      config: |
        #!/bin/sh
        (echo -n $(hostname -i); echo -n ' '; echo $(hostname)) > ${heat_outputs_path}.hosts

  export_hosts_sdg:
    type: OS::Heat::SoftwareDeploymentGroup
    properties:
      config: { get_resource: export_hosts }
      servers: { get_attr: [mpi_cluster, refs_map] }
      signal_transport: HEAT_SIGNAL

  populate_hosts:
    type: OS::Heat::SoftwareConfig
    properties:
      inputs:
        - name: hosts
      group: script
      config: |
        #!/usr/bin/env python
        import ast
        import os
        import subprocess
        hosts = os.getenv('hosts')
        if hosts is not None:
            hosts = ast.literal_eval(hosts.replace('\n', '\\n'))
        with open('/etc/hosts', 'a') as hosts_file:
          for ip_host in hosts.values():
              hosts_file.write(ip_host.rstrip() + '\n')

  populate_hosts_sdg:
    type: OS::Heat::SoftwareDeploymentGroup
    depends_on: export_hosts_sdg
    properties:
      config: { get_resource: populate_hosts }
      servers: { get_attr: [mpi_cluster, refs_map] }
      signal_transport: HEAT_SIGNAL
      input_values:
        hosts: { get_attr: [ export_hosts_sdg, hosts ] }

  mpi_cluster:
    type: OS::Heat::ResourceGroup
    properties:
      count: { get_param: node_count }
      resource_def:
        type: OS::Nova::Server
        properties:
          name: mpi-instance-%index%
          image: ANL-MPICH-3.3.1
          flavor: baremetal
          key_name: { get_param: key_name }
          networks:
             - network: sharednet1
          scheduler_hints: { reservation: { get_param: reservation_id } }
          user_data_format: SOFTWARE_CONFIG
          software_config_transport: POLL_SERVER_HEAT

          user_data:
            str_replace:
              template: |
                #!/bin/bash
                # disable HT
                for CPU in `seq 24 47`
                do
                   echo "0" > /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu$CPU/online;
                done
                sudo yum -y install wget

                # Take care of access key for instance
                cd /home/cc/.ssh/
                cat << EOF > id_rsa.pub
                public_key
                EOF
                cat << EOF > id_rsa
                private_key
                EOF
                cat << EOF > config
                Host *
                  StrictHostKeyChecking no
                EOF
                cat id_rsa.pub >> authorized_keys
                chmod 600 authorized_keys id_rsa
                chmod 644 id_rsa.pub config
                sudo chown cc:cc *

                cd /home/cc/
                for i in `seq 0 $(( node_count - 1 ))`
                do
                    echo mpi-instance-$i.novalocal >> hosts
                done
                sudo chown cc:cc hosts

                echo "export HYDRA_HOST_FILE=/home/cc/hosts" >> .bash_profile

                # mpirun_rsh -np 4 mpi-instance-0 mpi-instance-0 mpi-instance-0 mpi-instance-0 /usr/mpi/examples/graph500_mpi_one_sided 12

              params:
                node_count: { get_param: node_count }
                private_key: { get_attr: [ mpi_keypair, private_key ] }
                public_key: { get_attr: [ mpi_keypair, public_key ] }

outputs:
    first_instance_ip:
      description: The public IP address of the first instance. Login with the command 'ssh cc@first_instance_ip'.
      value: { get_attr: [instance_floating_ip, ip] }
    deployment_results:
      description: The private IPs and hostnames of all deployed instances
      value: { get_attr: [export_hosts_sdg, hosts] }

title: MPI+Spack KVM Cluster
short_description: This template sets up an HPC cluster with master and worker nodes, with MPI (MPICH and OpenMPI) and Spack available.
long_description:
This template sets up an HPC cluster with master and worker nodes, with MPI (MPICH and OpenMPI) and Spack available. A temporary bootstrap node handles the setup and configuration, and the users can load MPI or install/load other packages using Spack or Lmod(Lua Modules).

This appliance accepts the following parameters:

reservation_flavor: Flavor of the reservation for master and worker nodes.
bootstrapnode_reservation_flavor: Flavor of the reservation for the bootstrap node.
network_name: Name of the network.
image_name: Name of the image to be used by the cluster. Must be one of the following: Ubuntu22.04-HPC-MPI-Spack, Ubuntu22.04-HPC-MPI-Spack-CUDA, or Ubuntu22.04-HPC-MPI-Spack-ROCm. Defaults to Ubuntu22.04-HPC-MPI-Spack.
worker_count: Number of worker nodes. Defaults to 1.
spack_packages: List of additional Spack packages to install.
private_key_content: Contents of the SSH private key.
public_key_content: Contents of the SSH public key, allowing login into instances.
The following outputs are provided:

master_ip: Floating IP of the master node.
keypair_name: Name of the MPI keypair used.

ansible MPI MPICH openmpi

environment_setup.arguments:
heat_template_version: 2021-04-16

description: HPC cluster setup with Spack and MPI for deploying and configuring master and worker nodes via a bootstrap node.

parameters:
  bootstrapnode_reservation_flavor:
    type: string
    description: Flavor of the reservation for bootstrap node

  reservation_flavor:
    type: string
    description: Flavor of the reservation for master/workers

  network_name:
    type: string
    description: Network name (should be an existing one e.g. sharednet1)
    constraints:
      - custom_constraint: neutron.network

  image_name:
    type: string
    description: Image Name to be used by the cluster
    default: Ubuntu22.04-HPC-MPI-Spack

  worker_count:
    type: number
    description: Number of worker nodes
    default: 1

  spack_packages:
    type: comma_delimited_list
    description: List of Spack packages to install
    default: [ pdsh ]

  private_key_content:
    type: string
    description: SSH private key contents

  public_key_content:
    type: string
    description: SSH public key content, allows logging into instances

resources:

  mpi_ssh_sg:
    type: OS::Neutron::SecurityGroup
    properties:
      name: MPI-SSH-Access
      description: Allow inbound SSH traffic to all MPI instances
      rules:
        - protocol: tcp
          port_range_min: 22
          port_range_max: 22
          remote_ip_prefix: 0.0.0.0/0

  mpi_keypair:
    type: OS::Nova::KeyPair
    properties:
      name:
        list_join:
          - '-'
          - - { get_param: OS::stack_name }
            - keypair
      public_key: { get_param: public_key_content }

  bootstrap_node:
    type: OS::Nova::Server
    properties:
      name: mpi-bootstrap
      flavor: bootstrapnode_reservation_flavor 
      image: { get_param: image_name }
      key_name: { get_resource: mpi_keypair }
      networks:
        - network: { get_param: network_name }
      security_groups:
        - { get_resource: mpi_ssh_sg }
      user_data_format: RAW
      user_data:
        str_replace:
          template: |
            #!/bin/bash
            set -e

            mkdir -p /work/.ssh
            chown cc:cc /work/.ssh
            chmod 700 /work/.ssh

            cat > /work/.ssh/id_rsa <<EOF
            PRIVATE_KEY
            EOF

            cat > /work/.ssh/id_rsa.pub <<EOF
            PUBLIC_KEY
            EOF

            chmod 600 /work/.ssh/id_rsa
            chmod 644 /work/.ssh/id_rsa.pub
            chown -R cc:cc /work/.ssh

            apt-get update
            apt-get install -y git ansible

            cd /home/cc
            git clone https://github.com/pmodels/cc-hpc-appliances.git mpi-ansible
            cd mpi-ansible

            cat > inventory.ini <<EOF
            [master_node]
            MASTER_NAME ansible_host=MASTER_IP

            [worker_nodes]
            EOF

            IFS=',' read -r -a NAMES <<< "WORKER_NAMES"
            IFS=',' read -r -a IPS <<< "WORKER_IPS"
            for i in "${!NAMES[@]}"; do
              echo "${NAMES[$i]} ansible_host=${IPS[$i]}" >> inventory.ini
            done

            cat >> inventory.ini <<EOF
            [worker_nodes:vars]
            ansible_ssh_common_args='-o ProxyJump=cc@MASTER_IP'
            EOF
                        
            export ANSIBLE_PYTHON_INTERPRETER=/usr/bin/python3
            export ANSIBLE_SSH_ARGS="-F /home/cc/mpi-ansible/config"
            
            ansible-playbook -i ./inventory.ini -e "spack_packages=['SPACK_PACKAGES']" ./mpi-cluster.yml

          params:
            MASTER_NAME: { get_attr: [ master_node, name ] }
            MASTER_IP: { get_attr: [ master_floating_ip, ip ] }
            WORKER_NAMES: { list_join: [ ",", { get_attr: [ worker_nodes, name ] } ] }
            WORKER_IPS: { list_join: [ ",", { get_attr: [ worker_nodes, first_address ] } ] }
            PUBLIC_KEY: { get_param: public_key_content }
            PRIVATE_KEY: { get_param: private_key_content }
            SPACK_PACKAGES: { list_join: [ "','", { get_param: spack_packages } ] }

  master_node:
    type: OS::Nova::Server
    properties:
      name: mpi-master-node
      flavor: reservation_flavor
      image: { get_param: image_name }
      key_name: { get_resource: mpi_keypair }
      networks:
        - network: { get_param: network_name }
      security_groups:
        - { get_resource: mpi_ssh_sg }

  worker_nodes:
    type: OS::Heat::ResourceGroup
    properties:
      count: { get_param: worker_count }
      resource_def:
        type: OS::Nova::Server
        properties:
          name: mpi-worker-node-%index%
          flavor: reservation_flavor
          image: { get_param: image_name }
          key_name: { get_resource: mpi_keypair }
          networks:
            - network: { get_param: network_name }
          security_groups:
            - { get_resource: mpi_ssh_sg }

  master_floating_ip:
    type: OS::Nova::FloatingIP
    properties:
      pool: public

  master_floating_ip_association:
    type: OS::Nova::FloatingIPAssociation
    properties:
      floating_ip: { get_resource: master_floating_ip }
      server_id: { get_resource: master_node }

outputs:
  master_ip:
    description: Floating IP of the Master node
    value: { get_attr: [ master_floating_ip, ip ] }

  keypair_name:
    description: Name of the MPI KeyPair used
    value: { get_resource: mpi_keypair }

title: MPICH 3.3.1 (CentOS 7)
short_description: This appliance is built on top of CC-CentOS7.
long_description:
[Documentation](https://www.mpich.org/documentation/guides/)

This appliance is built on top of CC-CentOS7. It includes all Chameleon utilities, such as cc-checks, cc-snapshot, gnocchi collection agent, and cc-cloudfuse.

To run MPI programs, execute the following command, assuming you have compiled a program called mpi.out:

mpiexec -n <nprocs> -hostfile hosts ./mpi.out
To compile an MPI program, use a command such as this one:

mpicc -o hello_world hello_world.c
A simple program to compute the value of pi by numerical integration is included. You can run this program with:

mpiexec -n 4 cpi
Output should look like:

Process 0 of 4 is on mpich.novalocal
Process 1 of 4 is on mpich.novalocal
Process 3 of 4 is on mpich.novalocal
Process 2 of 4 is on mpich.novalocal
pi is approximately 3.1415926544231239, Error is 0.0000000008333307
wall clock time = 0.000164
There are many options for mpiexec, by which multiple executables can be run, hosts can be specified, separate command-line arguments and environment variables can be passed to different processes, and working directories and search paths for executables can be specified.

For more details, run:

mpiexec --help

title: RDMA-Hadoop + SR-IOV KVM Complex Appliance
short_description: The RDMA-Hadoop + SR-IOV KVM Complex Appliance is built based on OSU-CentOS7-KVM-SRIOV appliance
long_description:
[Documentation](https://www.chameleoncloud.org/appliances/45/docs/)

The RDMA-Hadoop + SR-IOV KVM Complex Appliance is built based on OSU-CentOS7-KVM-SRIOV appliance. With this appliance, users can run RDMA-Hadoop across VMs on SR-IOV enabled InfiniBand clusters.

Image name: OSU-CentOS7-RDMA-Hadoop-DIB
Default user account: cc
Remote access: Key-Based SSH
Root access: passwordless sudo from the cc account
Chameleon admin access: enabled on the ccadmin account
Cloud-init enabled on boot: yes
Repositories (Yum): EPEL, RDO (OpenStack)
Installed packages:
Rebuilt kernel to enable IOMMU
Mellanox SR-IOV drivers for InfiniBand
KVM hypervisor
Standard development tools such as make, gcc, gfortran, etc.
Config management tools: Puppet, Ansible, Salt
OpenStack command-line clients
Included VM image name: chameleon-rdma-hadoop-appliance.qcow2
Default VM root password: nowlab

RDMA-Hadoop SR-IOV

environment_setup.arguments:
heat_template_version: 2015-10-15

description: Hadoop cluster using KVM + SR-IOV and the RDMA-Hadoop library.
             Please make sure that you have leased a set of nodes with InfiniBand
             support before launching this complex appliance.

parameters:
  key_name:
    type: string
    label: Key name
    description: Name of a key pair to enable SSH access to the instance
    default: default
    constraints:
    - custom_constraint: nova.keypair
  reservation_id:
    type: string
    description: ID of the Blazar reservation to use for launching instances
    constraints:
    - custom_constraint: blazar.reservation

  total_nodes:
    type: number
    description: Number of slave hosts to launch. In addition to these nodes, one node will be used as the host for the Hadoop master node.
    default: 1
    constraints:
      - range: { min: 1 }
        description: There must be at least one physical node.
  total_vms:
    type: number
    description: Number of virtual machines (Hadoop slave nodes) to create. Should be a multiple of total_nodes.
    default: 1
    constraints:
      - range: { min: 1 }
        description: There must be at least one virtual machine.
  vcpu_per_vm:
    type: number
    description: Number of VCPUs per virtual machine
    default: 2
    constraints:
      - range: { min: 1 }
        description: There must be at least one vCPU per virtual machine.
  memory_per_vm:
    type: number
    description: Amount of memory size per virtual machine (in MB)

        user_data:
          str_replace:
            template: |

              cat << EOF > id_rsa

              EOF

              EOF

              chmod 600 authorized_keys id_rsa
              chmod 644 id_rsa.pub config
              sudo /bin/bash -c "cp /root/.ssh/id_rsa /root/.ssh/id_rsa.pub /root/.ssh/authorized_keys /root/.ssh/config /root/.ssh/"

              echo "Cluster Launch Complete!" >> /root/stack.log

Sage Project
The goal of the Sage project is to design and build a new kind of national-scale reusable cyberinfrastructure to enable AI at the edge. General Description
This image contains the appropriate software required to launch important and useful Sage services. With this image, users will be able to launch an instance of virtual waggle where users can create and run their own edge plugins for running machine and deep learning related tasks. This image is dynamic and new versions will be updated to Chameleon as soon as they are created. Older versions of the Sage image will be dated to the day they were created. environment_setup.arguments:
# This describes what is deployed by this template.
description: Ryu OpenFlow controller deployed with Heat on Chameleon

# This defines the minimum Heat version required by this template.
heat_template_version: ocata

# The resources section defines what OpenStack resources are to be deployed and
# how they should be configured.
resources:
  controller_floating_ip:
   type: OS::Nova::FloatingIP
   properties:
     pool: public

  controller:
   type: OS::Nova::Server
   properties:
     name: controller
     flavor: baremetal
     image: CC-CentOS8-stream
     key_name: { get_param: key_name }
     networks:
        - network: { get_param: controller_network_name }
     scheduler_hints: { reservation: { get_param: reservation_id } }
     user_data:
       str_replace:
         template: |
            #!/bin/bash
            {
            set -e -u -o pipefail

            RECIPE_REPO="https://github.com/RENCI-NRIG/exogeni-recipes.git"
            RECIPE_DIR="/opt/exogeni-recipes"
            RECIPE_APP="openflow-controller/docker"
            DOCKER_IMAGE="ryu-docker"
            DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME="ryu-controller"
            OFP_TCP_LISTEN_PORT="$ryu_port"
            RYU_APP="/opt/ryu_app/simple_switch_13_custom_chameleon.py"
            MIRROR_PORT="10000"

            sudo dnf install -y yum-utils device-mapper-persistent-data lvm2 vim

            echo "Installing Docker ..."
            sudo yum-config-manager --add-repo https://download.docker.com/linux/centos/docker-ce.repo
            sudo dnf install -y docker-ce
            sudo systemctl start docker

            echo "Configuring Ryu controller ..."
            git clone  --no-checkout $RECIPE_REPO $RECIPE_DIR
            cd $RECIPE_DIR && git config core.sparsecheckout true
            echo "$RECIPE_APP/*" >> .git/info/sparse-checkout
            git read-tree -m -u HEAD
            pushd ${RECIPE_DIR}/${RECIPE_APP}
            sed -r -i 's/^(RYU_APP=.*)/#\1/g' ryu_start.sh
            sed -r -i 's/^(OFP_TCP_LISTEN_PORT=.*)/#\1/g' ryu_start.sh

            echo "Building Ryu controller image ..."
            docker build -t ${DOCKER_IMAGE} .

            echo "Starting Ryu controller ..."
            docker run --rm -dit \
              -p $OFP_TCP_LISTEN_PORT:$OFP_TCP_LISTEN_PORT -p 8080:8080 \
              -v opt_ryu_chameleon:/opt/ryu_chameleon \
              -v opt_ryu:/opt/ryu \
              -v var_log_ryu:/var/log/ryu \
              -v var_run_ryu:/var/run/ryu \
              -e RYU_APP=$RYU_APP -e OFP_TCP_LISTEN_PORT=$OFP_TCP_LISTEN_PORT \
              --name=$DOCKER_CONTAINER_NAME \
              $DOCKER_IMAGE

            echo "Opening OF controller port ..."
            ufw allow $OFP_TCP_LISTEN_PORT

            echo "Done."
            } > /tmp/boot.log 2>&1
         params:
           $ryu_port: { get_param: controller_port }


  controller_ip_association:
    type: OS::Nova::FloatingIPAssociation
    properties:
      floating_ip: { get_resource: controller_floating_ip }
      server_id: { get_resource: controller }


parameters:
  key_name:
    type: string
    label: SSH Key
    description: Name of a KeyPair to enable SSH access to the instance
    constraints:
    - custom_constraint: nova.keypair

    label: Reservation
    type: string
    description: ID of the Blazar reservation to use for launching instances.
    constraints:
    - custom_constraint: blazar.reservation
  controller_network_name:
    type: string
    label: Controller Node Network
    description: Name of the network used by the controller. NOT the new OpenFlow netork.
    default: sharednet1
    constraints:
    - custom_constraint: neutron.network
  controller_port:
    type: string
    label: OpenFlow Controller Port
    description: The port used by the OpenFlow controller.
    default: 6653

  parameters:
  - controller_network_name
  - controller_port
- label: General Configuration
  description: General parameters
  parameters:
  - key_name
  - reservation_id

environment_setup.arguments:
# This describes what is deployed by this template.
description: Ryu OpenFlow controller deployed with Heat on Chameleon

# This defines the minimum Heat version required by this template.
heat_template_version: ocata

# The resources section defines what OpenStack resources are to be deployed and
# how they should be configured.
resources:
  controller_floating_ip:
   type: OS::Nova::FloatingIP
   properties:
     pool: public

  controller_ip_association:
    type: OS::Nova::FloatingIPAssociation
    properties:
      floating_ip: { get_resource: controller_floating_ip }
      server_id: { get_resource: controller }

  controller:
   type: OS::Nova::Server
   properties:
     name: controller
     flavor: baremetal
     image: CC-CentOS7
     key_name: { get_param: key_name }
     networks:
        - network: { get_param: controller_network_name }
     scheduler_hints: { reservation: { get_param: reservation_id } }
     user_data:
       str_replace:
         template: |
           #!/bin/bash

           WORKING_DIR=/root
           {
           CHAMELEON_RYU_URL="https://github.com/ChameleonCloud/ryu.git"
           CHAMELEON_RYU_APP="mirror_switch_13_chameleon.py"

           yum install -y epel-release
           yum install -y python-pip git
           pip install ryu
           pip install --upgrade pip
           # Remedy some version conflicts
           # These packages are already installed, ryu installation requirements are satisfied, but running the
           # code generates errors with existing versions of six and netaddr. Needs to be updated.
           pip install --upgrade six
           pip install --upgrade --ignore-installed netaddr

           useradd openflow
           usermod -s /sbin/nologin openflow

           RYU_DIR="/opt/ryu"

           mkdir ${RYU_DIR} && mkdir ${RYU_DIR}/repo

           # Ryu Application file that is customized for Chameleon use-case
           #wget http://geni-images.renci.org/images/mcevik/openflow/ryu/simple_switch_13_custom_chameleon.py
           curl http://geni-images.renci.org/images/pruth/ryu/${CHAMELEON_RYU_APP}  > ${RYU_DIR}/${CHAMELEON_RYU_APP}
           git clone ${CHAMELEON_RYU_URL} ${RYU_DIR}/repo

           chown -R openflow. ${RYU_DIR}
           mkdir /var/run/ryu
           chown openflow. /var/run/ryu
           mkdir /var/log/ryu
           chown openflow. /var/log/ryu


           cat << EOF > /etc/sysconfig/ryu
           RYU_PID_FILE="/var/run/ryu/ryu-manager.pid"
           RYU_LOG_FILE="/var/log/ryu/ryu-manager.log"
           RYU_CONFIG_DIR="/opt/ryu/etc"
           RYU_APP="${RYU_DIR}/${CHAMELEON_RYU_APP}"
           OFP_TCP_LISTEN_PORT="$ryu_port"
           EOF


           cat << EOF > /etc/systemd/system/ryu.service
           [Unit]
           Description=Ryu Openflow Controller Service
           After=network.target

           [Service]
           EnvironmentFile=/etc/sysconfig/ryu
           User=openflow
           ExecStart=/usr/bin/ryu-manager --pid-file \${RYU_PID_FILE} --ofp-tcp-listen-port \${OFP_TCP_LISTEN_PORT} --log-file \${RYU_LOG_FILE} \${RYU_APP}
           KillMode=process
           Restart=on-abort

           [Install]
           WantedBy=multi-user.target
           EOF

           cat << EOF > /etc/logrotate.d/ryu
           /var/log/ryu/*.log {
               rotate 2
               missingok
               nocreate
               sharedscripts
               size 100M
               compress
               postrotate
                   /bin/systemctl restart ryu.service 2> /dev/null || true
               endscript
           }
           EOF

           # https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/systemd-tmpfiles.html
           cat << EOF > /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/ryu.conf
           d /var/run/ryu 0775 root openflow
           EOF

           systemctl enable ryu
           systemctl daemon-reload
           systemctl restart ryu
           systemctl status ryu
           } > ${WORKING_DIR}/boot.log 2>&1
         params:
           $ryu_port: { get_param: controller_port }

  security_onion_floating_ip:
   type: OS::Nova::FloatingIP
   properties:
     pool: public

  security_onion_ip_association:
    type: OS::Nova::FloatingIPAssociation
    properties:
      floating_ip: { get_resource: security_onion_floating_ip }
      server_id: { get_resource: security_onion }

  security_onion:
    depends_on: controller
    type: OS::Nova::Server
    properties:
      name: security_onion
      flavor: baremetal
      image: CC-Ubuntu16.04 
      key_name: { get_param: key_name }
      networks:
             - network: { get_resource: of_network }
      scheduler_hints: { reservation: { get_param: reservation_id } }
      user_data:
        str_replace:
          template: |
            #!/bin/bash
            WORKING_DIR=/root
            {
            echo "nameserver 8.8.8.8" >> /etc/resolv.conf
            #while true; do
            #   echo trying to ping...
            #    ping -c 1 github.com > /dev/null 2>&1
            #
            #    if [[ $? -eq 0 ]]; then
            #        break
            #   fi
            #done
                        
            RECIPE_REPO="https://github.com/RENCI-NRIG/exogeni-recipes.git"
            RECIPE_DIR="/opt/exogeni-recipes"
            RECIPE_APP="security-onion"
            RECIPE_FILE="so-install.sh"
            
            WHITELIST=$domain
            SO_ANSWER_FILE="sosetup_answerfile_for_chameleon_node"
            git clone  --no-checkout ${RECIPE_REPO} ${RECIPE_DIR}
            cd ${RECIPE_DIR} && git config core.sparsecheckout true
            echo "${RECIPE_APP}/" >> .git/info/sparse-checkout
            git read-tree -m -u HEAD
            chmod +x ${RECIPE_DIR}/${RECIPE_APP}/${RECIPE_FILE}
            while `lsof /var/lib/dpkg/lock` || `lsof /var/cache/debconf/templates.dat`; do 
                sleep 1 
            done && ${RECIPE_DIR}/${RECIPE_APP}/${RECIPE_FILE}
            
            if [ -x /usr/sbin/sosetup ]; then
                echo "--- Apply Workaround for delays on Pulledpork rule-updates"
                sed -i -r "s/(^.*&& INTERNET=)\"UP\"/\1\"DOWN\"/g" /usr/sbin/sosetup
                echo "--- Start configuring the node with the answerfile"
                /usr/sbin/sosetup -f ${RECIPE_DIR}/${RECIPE_APP}/${SO_ANSWER_FILE} -y
            fi 
            echo "--- Add firewall rule for ${WHITELIST}"
            ufw allow proto tcp from ${WHITELIST} to any port 443,22,7734 
            } > ${WORKING_DIR}/install_security_onion.log 2>&1
          params:
            $domain: { get_param: domain }

environment_setup.arguments:
